I spent 25 days in Bentota, and by the time I left, it felt less like a holiday destination and more like a second home. Bentota is one of those rare places in Sri Lanka where you can completely slow down, but still have plenty to see and do if you want more than just beach time. Most mornings started at Bentota Beach, enjoying the sun, sea, and long stretches of golden sand. Even during peakù busy days, the beach never felt crowded, and the calm atmosphere made it perfect for long walks, swimming, or simply doing nothing at all. One of the highlights of my stay was exploring the Bentota River and mangrove lagoon. The river safari was peaceful and scenic, and stopping for a fish spa along the way was a surprisingly relaxing experience. For a bit more excitement, I also tried water sports, which are well organised and suitable for both beginners and more adventurous travellers. Bentota is also rich in nature and culture. I visited the Turtle Sanctuary, which was both educational and heart-warming, especially seeing the conservation work being done. A visit to a low-country tea estate gave me a new appreciation for Sri Lankan tea, while exploring the moonstone mines was fascinating and something quite unique to this region. Architecture and spirituality are also part of Bentota’s charm. Walking through Geoffrey Bawa’s botanical gardens was a real highlight — beautifully designed and very peaceful. I also visited the Kande Vihara ancient temple, which has an impressive presence and offers a calm, reflective atmosphere. I spent a few days exploring nearby areas too. Cinnamon Island (Mirala Duwa) was a must-visit, where locals demonstrated how real Ceylon cinnamon is grown and processed. Early mornings at Beruwala Fishing Harbour gave a glimpse into local life, and a short visit to the Beruwala Lighthouse offered lovely views of the coastline. One memorable outing was a boat ride to Troll Rock during low tide, which felt like discovering a hidden spot. Other experiences included visiting spice gardens, learning about the essential properties of Sri Lankan spices, and watching locals create traditional woodwork and handcrafted masks, which really shows the depth of local craftsmanship. For nature lovers, the hike up Pahuru Kanda (Little Adam’s Peak) was rewarding, and cooling off afterward at Polgampola Waterfall and its natural pool was the perfect way to end the day. Food was a big part of my experience in Bentota, and one place stood out throughout my stay — Esprit Seafood Restaurant and Bar. Despite the name, the menu is very diverse, making it suitable for everyone. Alongside excellent seafood, they also serve well-prepared steaks, chicken dishes, vegetarian options, and meals catering to different dietary needs. The restaurant is set in a peaceful location, and many evenings were made even better with live music such as saxophone or acoustic guitar, creating a relaxed and welcoming atmosphere. It’s easy to understand why Esprit has earned a TripAdvisor Travellers’ Choice Award — the consistency in food quality, service, and ambiance really shows. After spending nearly a month in Bentota, what stood out most was the balance it offers — beach, adventure, culture, nature, and great food, all without feeling rushed or overcrowded. It’s a destination that suits couples, families, and long-stay travellers alike. I left feeling refreshed and already looking forward to returning.

Bentota Beach is one of Sri Lanka’s most popular coastal destinations, known for its golden sands, calm turquoise waters, and relaxed tropical atmosphere. Located on the southwest coast, it is ideal for both leisure and adventure. Visitors can enjoy sunbathing, swimming, and romantic beach walks, while the nearby Bentota River offers exciting water sports such as jet skiing, banana boat rides, and river safaris. The area is also famous for luxury resorts, ayurvedic spas, and beautiful sunsets. With easy access from Colombo, Bentota Beach is perfect for families, couples, and travelers seeking a peaceful seaside escape.

One of the cleanest and widest beaches in Sri Lanka, all the water sports and beach sports could be done here also wanted to highlight below attraction The Mythical Troll Rock of Bentota Beach: Handirangala – A Sleeping Giant in the Ocean Nestled along the golden shores of Bentota Beach, Sri Lanka, lies an enigmatic natural formation steeped in mystery and legend. Known locally as Handirangala, this unique rock formation has captivated locals and travelers alike with its striking resemblance to a sleeping giant. Rising above the tranquil waters of the Indian Ocean, Handirangala is more than just a geological wonder; it is a testament to the fusion of nature’s artistry and the rich folklore of Sri Lanka. The Legend of Handirangala According to local lore, Handirangala, or “The Troll Rock,” is the petrified remains of a mythical giant. The story recounts how this giant once roamed the island with unmatched strength and a deep connection to nature. However, driven by hubris or love for the ocean, he defied the gods and was cursed to eternal slumber. Over centuries, the waves and wind sculpted his body into the rocky outcrop visible today, where he rests as a silent guardian of the shore. Some say that during certain times of the day, when the sunlight hits the rock just right, the giant’s features—his forehead, nose, and chin—become unmistakably clear, evoking awe and wonder. The Geological Marvel Beyond the myth, Handirangala is a fascinating geological formation. Composed of ancient rock, likely shaped by volcanic activity and centuries of coastal erosion, it serves as a reminder of the Earth’s evolving landscape. The rock’s contours mimic the form of a reclining figure, with its “head” pointing toward the sky and its “body” merging seamlessly into the ocean. This natural phenomenon highlights the interplay between geology and human imagination, as people have long found stories within the patterns of the earth. The Mystique from the Beach From the soft, golden sands of Bentota Beach, the silhouette of Handirangala is unmistakable. The tranquility of the setting adds to the mystique of the rock, as the ocean waves lap gently against its base, echoing the whispers of ancient tales. Visitors often find themselves lost in thought, marveling at how nature can evoke such humanlike forms. For photographers and nature enthusiasts, the rock provides a perfect subject, particularly during sunrise and sunset, when the interplay of light and shadow accentuates its shape. A Symbol of Cultural and Natural Heritage Handirangala is not just a visual spectacle but a cultural symbol. The rock embodies the deep-rooted relationship between Sri Lankans and their environment, where myths breathe life into natural landmarks. It also serves as a reminder of the need to preserve such sites for future generations. The allure of Handirangala attracts visitors from all over the world, making it an integral part of Bentota’s charm and a must-visit destination for those exploring Sri Lanka. Conclusion Handirangala, the mythical Troll Rock of Bentota Beach, is a place where legend and nature converge. Its mysterious allure and breathtaking presence inspire imagination and reverence, offering a glimpse into the profound ways humanity connects with its surroundings. Whether as a geological wonder, a cultural landmark, or a mythological relic, this sleeping giant continues to watch over the shimmering waters of the Indian Ocean, inviting all who visit to dream, explore, and believe in the magic of the natural world.

I recently had a wonderful trip to Bentota, an amazing stretch of beach on Sri Lanka's southern coast. It’s a favourite spot of mine that I visit whenever I can with my family, since it’s just about 1.5 hours from home. Our latest visit was extra special with high tea at Rock Villa Bentota. Bentota Beach truly is a gem, offering a perfect mix of natural beauty and relaxation. The golden sands extend for miles, gently caressed by the Indian Ocean’s waves. It’s a great place for swimming, sunbathing, or enjoying water sports like jet skiing and windsurfing. The sunsets here are simply spectacular, with the sky glowing in shades of orange and pink, creating a magical atmosphere. Whether you're seeking a peaceful escape or some adventure, Bentota Beach has something special for everyone.

Bentota Beach Hotel, an icon in Sri Lankan architecture and a property with a rich history reconstructed by Bawa’s student, Channa Daswatte is a true tribute to Sri Lanka’s most famed architect Geoffrey Bawa. Standing on the balcony of the Geoffrey Bawa Suite, you see the sea on the right and the Bentota river on the left, and Sripada and the central hills on the far right, all in one view. This view, according to architect Channa Daswatte makes this property the one that links the land and the sea. The ‘new’ Bentota Beach is not merely a recreation or a restoration. The main building of the old hotel has been reconstructed newly, as it was built by Bawa. This showcases Bawa’s wide  architectural influences ranging from Bali to ancient Sri Lankan monuments. Inside the hotel has the signature of Geoffrey Bawa and the period it was constructed in, but in a modern and functional representation. The lead architect Channa Daswatte has done an amazing job, not only to archive an iconic construction but also through his brilliance, make it a fresh, modern and functional. It is a museum and treasure trove of art and architecture, that concurrently delivers a guests expectections from a modern luxury hotel.

Let’s read a little google knowledge about the place before I narrate further Bentota is a resort town on Sri Lanka’s southwest coast. Its long Bentota Beach stretches north, where it becomes a sandy strip known as Paradise Island, parallel to Bentota Lagoon. Coral-rich dive sites include Canoe Rock. On Bentota River, centuries-old Galapota Temple has a large Buddha statue. Together with the smaller Randombe Lake, to which Bentota lake is connected by two narrow channels, it forms the Madu Ganga wetland. Its estuary and the many mangrove islets on it constitute a complex coastal wetland ecosystem. In has high ecological, biological and aesthetic significance, being home to approximately 303 species of plants belonging to 95 families and to 248 species of vertebrate animals. The inhabitants of its islets produce peeled cinnamon and cinnamon oil. The Maduganga Wetland was declared in 2003, in terms of the Ramsar Convention. The Budha statue , the temple in the river and people making their livelihood through Cinnamon oil production in various island of a total of sixty two islands in the river made us happy and the sadness of turtle accidents reduced it a bit.  Spotting monitor lizard , few white and black birds ( photos attached) and purple faced monkeys brought wider smiles on everyone’s face. Fish foot massage was another activity if the day. The experts say the health risks, both to humans and to the fish, outweigh any potential benefits. Great beach (the best we've seen in Sri Lanka, out of 4 or 5) IF: 1) you don't want bars and annoying vendors on the beach, 2) you don't like crowds, 3) you like fine-grained sand and a clean beach, 4) especially, if you like swimming – not wading, but really swimming. There is a rock between the bay and the sea, it's about 900 meters from the beach, so it's a great swim.  When the sea is calm, you can swim very near the rock and see all kinds of fish (not much of coral reef, though, and whatever there is is dead).  When the sea is not so calm, be very careful – I stayed at least 10–20 meters away from the nearest visible rock, and I could still see some rocks beneath me. The downsides: 1) The sea is very opaque (cloudy) – you can't see further than 1 meter, perhaps a little more.  This is because of the very fine sand floating in the sea (near the beach) and, above all, because of microscopic algae making the water green.  2) On the way from the beach to the rock, there is an area where somewhat dirty-looking foam gathers – you might want to swim around it.  3) Of course, as transpires from the above, if you like beach partying, this is not a beach for you.  4) The waves can be strong, so I am not sure it's a good beach for small kids.

We gave it a three because you can’t swim in the water and some rubbish can be found when going for a walk. It is cleaner than most Asian beaches and the sand is lovely to walk on.

A must visit to anyone coming to Sri Lanka this is a very long beautiful clean beach with a lot of surf and also other activities for individual travelers or Family Travel. 2 hrs drive from Colombo city or Colombo International Airport

One of the better and quietest beaches we found.

Our hotel The Surf was just on the beach The beach is clean with clear blue water sea. I had a swim too in the sea.. You can see a lot of jogger’s both in the morning and the evening. Saw coast guards meticulously monitoring the beach. Very nice experience.
Lovely staff, beautiful hotel, staff can't do enough for you, very very clean, food good and beach is amazing. Can't fault it at all.

I was over emphasized by my travel agent to visit Bentota Beach. Bentota is a coastal town in Sri Lanka, located in the Galle District of the Southern Province, governed by an Urban Council. It is approximately 65 kilometres (40 mi) south of Colombo and 56 kilometres (35 mi) north of Galle. Bentota is situated on the southern bank of the Bentota River mouth, at an elevation of 3 metres (9.8 ft) above the sea level. The name of the town is derived from a mythical story which claims a demon named 'Bem' ruled the tota or river bank. we were want to Bentota I was wondering. the beach was rally really nice. Lovely beach and beautiful sunset.

It's nothing like the best beach in Sri Lanka but it's perfectly pleasant. 2km long to the north of the Taj hotel (there's an even longer beach to the south not explored). It has a wide expanse of light beige sand varying from 20-60 metres wide above the tide mark with a palm tree fringe behind. At low tide the wet sand is hard and easy to walk on. There are no eat or drink facilities on the beach. There are several hotels to the south (Taj, Surf, Loft) but apart from these there's not much else. A couple of water sports facilities, hire of beds and umbrellas (200-400rps per day). At the south end near the hotels it's quite busy but north it's almost deserted. Walk to the north end and you can cut across to the river estuary. There's also a path up to a sweet Buddhist temple at the top of the rocks with great views (remove shoes at top of climb). Well worth the walk but take a bottle of water.

Nice vibrant beach with beach sport activities. Lots of high end restaurants by the beach and one can indulge in a variety of sea food.
We only went to the beach along the Centara Ceysands and it was a brilliant beach with fine sand, blue waters and no people to intrude on you!
We stayed in surf hotel and it's on the beach, just 2 min walk and you are in the beach. Good clean beach and have done a morning walk over there

We went there on a casual Sunday during September. The beach is clean and the sand is so smooth. The red flags were up but still we could have a great sea bath. Lifeguards were there and we kept our belongings on the sand and it was safe. Considering it's not far from Colombo, an ideal

We visited Bentota beach while we were in the Bentota Beach Hotel. It is nice beach in the western side of Sri Lanka. Once you are on the beach you can watch the sun set. The sea is not rough but it may be little rough during the southwest monsoon period that is mid-May to September. During October November due the sea breeze effect sea may be rough from 1400 hours to about 2000 hours. Sea is very light during December to February that is during the North East Monsoon period. During North East Monsoon period Seas in the Eastern side of Sri Lanka will be rough. Except for the period May to September seas in the western side of Sri Lanka is good for sea bathing.

This beach is lovely. Albeit the water a little choppy... but good for surfing I imagine. Watch out for the men who start walking with you and end up being some kind of tour guide as they recommend places who only want your money (standard). Beach itself is stunning.
Miles of sand no one to bother you just waves sand and wildlife.all this after the sunarmi what a great job they have done
Its unbelievably clean! the sand so soft you can walk barefoot, and won't feel a thing. a definite must go. water sports are good too.

The tourist season is clearly over in September. There were just a few locals and tourists on the beach. A few salesmen walked up and down. The sea was rough and the mostly empty resorts had red flags out. Swimming was possible and even fun, but too dangerous to go beyond where you could still stand on the bottom. Sun was still scorching hot. Besides the beach there is really nothing else to do here.

Your rating of this beach would depend entirely on where you live. Being fortunate enough to live in Australia, any beach overseas is always a disappointment but this one is lovely to look at and it is clean. The hotel staff at the various places along here constantly have signs up warning that this beach is unsafe for swimming and no doubt for many people it would be. But again when your local beach is one of the most dangerous in Australia (if not the world) on Victoria's Mornington Peninsula with regular six foot waves and rips that cause more than 100 surf live saving rescues per year then most overseas beaches are a doddle in comparison and I was hoping for much bigger waves to have a good body surf. In fact it is mostly choppy with the odd rip but then not the undertow you see in many other beaches in the world but the water is very warm - which makes it quite pleasant - and importantly there are no sharks, stingers or crocodiles (in contrast to Aussie beaches).
Lovely beach but you must adhere to any sea warnings these are put out by hotels along beach front. Also people touting for trips if you say no they do not bother you
It was such an amazing journey to wake up on the amazing sea view. I advise you to stay at the Surf.
Just carry a book, couple of drinks, and a snack. Its calm, not crowded, Relax looking at the sea! Do not litter :)

Lovely clean long sandy beach, check tides for when you visit August not good for people who like to venture into the sea very rough double red flag, still amazing to sit in the sun and watch the beautiful waves lapping the shore and feel that breeze
Vivanta by Taj straddles two long sandy beaches, so just pick one and head off for a long walk and a swim.
We visited Bentota during the off season, so it may be different at other times, but the beach really needs a regular cleanup.

This is my second visit to this lovely beach of Bentota. I would say it is one of a kind. The beach is always clean and you can live some unforgettable moments through out the day especially during sunset. The only bothersome issue here is the boring offers from some locals for water-sports. I would strongly recommend resisting such random offers to enjoy the moment.
Lovely beach to visit n hang out with the family. Clean unspoiled beautiful beach. We were a large group n enjoyed treading waves

Nothing is similar to the sunset and the endless horizon view of the Indian Ocean. Clean and soft sand beaches with lots of nice hotels and with  long shallow beaches. Perfect for a relaxing retreat and you have 10s of options for water sports offered by the beach boys.
Even when it wasn't the season and not summer, but this beautiful beach was a perfect place for chilling out and spending 2 days on its warm sand relaxing
When you run on the beach in the morning, it is so beautiful The sunset is great and it is not over crowed at all
The sand is soft and warm beneath your feet...The water is warm and the breeze is brisk...A perfect place for a morning run! A must see in Bentota!

This is such a beautiful Beach, we a family of four enjoyed the lovely soft sand the water this time of year is a bit rough but that didn't stop our enjoyment, the beach sellers are not a put off (friendly smile and polite no thank you) and they walk on, the occasional beach dog is also a nice touch, most days we where the only ones on Bentota Beach, weekends locals come down to enjoy the sunsets and kite flying adds to all a really enjoyable time

The moment of my visit was end of June, when the Indian Ocean waters are black and agitated, especially since this year's floods affected lots of the western coast side too. But the amazing colors were a photographer's dream. The water reflecting as almost back and the foam white, seemed like the ocean was made of coffee.

The sand is lovely and soft and golden. The beach is clean and the ocean and views are great. Nice restaurants in Bentota and lovely people. Just be careful of the ocean, watch for the flags as it can be very rough with strong currents.
Nice beach, wild sea in August so swimming can be dangerous. The rent waveboards at the beach wich is fun to do with kids

Terrible stay.  Rude staff, especially the manager, poor quality of rooms (holes in blinds, peeling paint, warning signs on door - all photographed). Wedding planner was rarely in which led to mass confusion and made our wedding less the event it should have been.  5 times we asked over 2 days to get a wedding menu.  She kindly suggested we married at 1000 hrs (33 degrees c+) when we had asked for 1630 hrs as it was cooler. Photographer took 100 photos (apx 80% had my/my wife/or both our eyes closed).  Real let down and very upsetting on our special day. I reported issues to the Manager who did not rectify a single one.  Saman HQ offered no apology for our mistreatment. A waste of money and time.  We certainly could not recommend this place or ever plan to return.  Really poor.  Reminiscent of Fawlty Towers in a 3* hotel with 2* service.
The Bentota beach is another spot for ralaxed walking, swimming or just lying on the beach enjoying the warn sun.  There is also some water sports near by in the lake

I would not recommend snorkelling here or planning to snorkel as the sea is very rough at times and it can be hard to paddle in it. I would not recccomend trying to swim in it unless you know how to 'body surf' etc
long clean beach with soft sand ,not too much crowded is the best part of this place,in off season hardly any ppl and no shop, restaurants, so will suggest to visit in proper season

Neat and clean beach , not too much crowded . long beach , enjoy the walking and explore the beach with your loved ones . only few km away from colombo airport . people who like peace this is the best place  relax enjoy the surrounding .

The beach itself is quite nice. Some days it looked cleaner than others (2 week stay) so someone must be cleaning it all be it infrequently. There is some hassle from guides, sellers and restaurants but this is minimal and a quick no thank you and they drop it. The huge issue I have as a western woman is the vile groups of men who think it's acceptable to leer and gawk at you. They are so blatant and don't care if you give them a disapproving look. I even shouted and gestured to why don't the take a picture and they still stare. It's disgusting and totally unacceptable. I was with my husband so wasn't a lone female but I can't imagine how terrifying it would be if you were. I believe the men in question are Indian groups, I had exactly the same issue in Goa. Never had this issue in Thailand or Bali. Really off putting.
Wide long beach with nice soft sand. Unfortunately there is no restaurant or shop. Out of main season without many people.

The beach is very clean; you can walk around and see sunset (if no clouds). It's around 80 Km ( 1.5 hours) from Colombo airport and has a express way to reach from Colombo to Bentota. During rainy season there are chances of high tide, so you may not get a chance to go into water and do swimming. Overall nice beach to visit if you are in Sri Lanka!!
Nice sand very pleasant to walk apart from being stopped by a few beach boys who tried to walk you to certain places. Just ignore them
The beach is clean practically stoneless and the ocean is pleasantly warm. This creamy white beach was excellent for strolling along any time of day or night
Lovely weather in August. Waves are a little rough but warm and sandy. No rocks. Few travel agents walking the beach front that can be annoying but friendly 😊.
Nice beach. Very stormy in August. Swimming not possible then. We stayed at nearby Saman Villas, which we recommend.
Lovely beach but the sea is very rough; nice place though for a stop-over for lunch or some pictures

One of the best beaches i have been to, swimming in the ocean was super pleasant and fun,  i would recommend that you walk/take tok tok to go all the way to the end of the beach where the sea meats the river, unforgettable scenes
Stunning beach but unable to enter sea due to dangerous currents. Some people a nuisance on beach claiming to work in hotel and know you wanting to take you to shops etc
Not the best option in srilanka but there are better options across the country. But while in the city do visit and spend a evening here.
A beach that stretches on for miles and golden clean sand with huge high breaking waves of the Indian Ocean.
It's a long and clean beach.... lovely to walk barefoot in the wet sands. Towards the end on both sides of the beach are some upmarket hotels and restaurants for beach/sea view eating experience.
This is a beautiful stretch of sand and sea. Although it was the off season, so the sea is too rough to swim, we could still paddle in clear water and walk along really soft sand.

During raining season there is not much to do. And watch out for The Beach Boys. They are friendly at first and give you food and drinks but they have other meaning. I heard that people woke up later and didn't know what happened and lost there stuff. Also I heard they try to convince girls to have sex. Sometimes they even put things in your drink. It just what I heard also from local people. So just be careful. Also there were no terraces or bars on the beach. The sunset on the other hand is amazing and when I was there you could swim. It also has a rescue brigade which is good.

This beach is absolutely beautiful, lovely powder soft sand, palm trees my idea of paradise. Very quiet, not many people on it, locals are all very nice. No one selling goods either so you relax and enjoy. Water lovely and warm , waves can be quite big , also current quite strong in places think it's to do with the tide,so a watchful eye must be kept on any children. Only problem is plastic- the locals have an ongoing battle as every tide brings in more ! They do a marvellous job clearing it up.

I walked both adjoining beaches several times it is good physical exercise not due to the distance but just hard to avoid the soft sand which makes the going a bit tougher. I loved the setting of this beach only a handful of resorts and bars set up along its entire length (approx 4km) other places I have visited in Asia would have 150+ and have destroyed the landscape and cleanliness of the water. Rugged, natural, foreboding and plenty of wildlife to enjoy if you get lucky, also a few bars and restaurants to stop on route. There is sadly a bit of trash washed up in places but again nothing compared to what I have seen in other Asian countries and I can see locals are cleaning up what is mainly plastic bottles tossed overboard by fishermen I suspect - I think I am lucky and have come at a good time I hope it does not change to quickly.
A wide expanse of beach, which was very clean and great to walk along. You can walk for quite a distance along this stretch undisturbed.
What amazed me was the cleanliness maintained on the beach. Not a lot of people..but loads of choice for hotel and restaurants. The only minus point is that the sand is extremely fine

This is a beautiful location and a fantastic place to watch the sunset, however it does have at times some rubbish washed ashore, if only this could be cleaned more often it would be a five-star beach. A nice walk can be had to a magical temple on a small island to the right as you look out to sea.
Does need a bit of cleaning but on the whole breathtakingly beautiful. Nice to walk on to see the temple
Looked nice but raw sewage evident in areas. Red flags up throughout stay but not keen to enter sea based on health risk of sewage

During the wet season the water is a dark brown colour due to the rainfall. Besides the rubbish and other residue, the water is very warm. Waves were on shore and messy but you can still find some fun right handers in the south corner next to the point.
Beautiful beach but be careful... on certain days there was raw sewage being extracted directly into the sea

The waves are good for surfers and a mesmerising sight for non surfers. Ocean here is a beautiful pristine blue. Do make sure you are then in the evening! So beautiful and so relaxing. A lovely atmosphere too
The waves are high and great for surfing and playing around. Of course the sun in Srilanka is torturous so enjoy the early mornings and evenings. warm ocean and lots of bars and restaurants around.
The beach is very clean,  the ocean is very strong this time of the year.  We have a very nice time here in Sri Lanka.  We will come back here next for a two week visit.

Great for long walks. we had no trouble with people trying to sell  us stuff. The sea was rough whilst we were there in June. But I don't think it's ever safe to swim in the sea along this stretch of coast. Really beautiful and cooler than inland.

Bentota beach is not suitable for kids not adults swimming. It's mainly for surfers. We didn't like the beach and the sea much as we are comparing it with the breathtaking beaches that we have visited  in Phuket, Bali, Dubai etc.

This was the best beach ( clean, absolutely no crowd, place to have a shower & change) amongst all the beaches that I visited during my Sri Lanka Holiday. The beach is just across the road when you reach Bentota by train. The moment you reach the beach/bentota station you will be approcahed by friendly boys who try to sell you adventure sports, the Bentota Rive safari etc. Tip: Negotiate the price if you opt for any of the offerings from the friendly beach guides
Lovely lovely beach , keep an eye out for the facinating wildlife and the lovely friendly dogs. It's just how I imagined paradise to be
This is the most amazing place in Bentota. This is a very clean paradis. Very matches areas for photography and spend leisure time.

The beach is lovely if you want to see the sunset. Have coconut water available outside, sit on the sand, sip water and watch the sun go down. Bentota beach will offer you the cherished pleasures of life.
Its a very clean beach. Enjoyed long stretches of walk by the side, collecting loads of seashells and playing with waves! Too relaxing, had a great time!
Lovely sandy beach with no rocks or sea weed. Sea was rough when we went (april/may), but didn't put us off going in. Currents are strong though.

We managed to go to Sri Lanka as the terrible monsoons hit therefore the water was rough and the beach was full of debris that had been washed up and from the rivers. This was disappointing but mother nature is unpredictable.
Good place to stay with friends and family. Service excellent ,buffet food was good pool bar a la cart food was okay, what we expected we couldn't get.overall we like

We were here in June 2017 and this was just the start of their monsoons. The beaches were clean and neat and less crowded. We couldn't enjoy any water sports  on the beach due to high tide, but you can enjoy the rides on the lagoon nearby.

Bentota has a beautiful beach. I traveled in Oct/Nov and was instructed not to go swimming due to the high current. However, its a perfect beach for long walks and there seems to be some areas that have inlets where the tide isn't was strong and we saw people in the water.

The beach is massive however I thought the stretch to left past the rocks was better than the section where the big resort hotels are. The resort section did not have restaurants or bars on the beach and the beach had sand flies and sales people who pestered us a little bit. Bentota town is pretty pants there is nothing really there. Sea was very very dangerous as it is monsoon season but that is just the way it is.

Our hotel was right on the beach and we spent quite a lot of time on the beach. It is very clean and calm. Around weekends the beach gets a little crowded though. There are lots of hotels on the beach but no options to eat/restaurants though. You can also find water sports activities and other activities like motor parasailing etc. Its on the west coast so sunsets are pretty good.
The sandy beach seemed to go on for ever and we could see the beautiful sunsets over it. the sea was a bit rough.
May Is certainly not the seasons to visit beaches at Sri Lanka. Walks by the beach when sea is rough were really soothing , had good time at resort with family.
Due to monsoon season the sea was extremely rough and many rip tides in place, red flags consultants flying. Beach was also not the cleanest with litter being washed up and not removed

Lovely quiet beach big expanse of sand, worth walking up to the left and round the corner. Hardly anyone there lovely. There was a lady picking up litter - this was the only place we saw this happen on the island but it was so appreciated - later in the trip we went to Tangalle and it was full of rubbish horrible. We arrived by taxi from the airport 2 hours to a lovely guesthouse Aayu's highly recommended. Easy walk to the beach and we enjoyed a beer at the Loft bar on the beach but take a drink with you if you walk further up as nothing there. We left by train from Bentota to Matara for our onward travels 2 hours less than a fiver for 3 of us. On reflection we should have headed back to Bentota on our last night as only 2 hours from the airport but we made the mistake of going to Negombo as near to the airport but it was depressing with a filthy beach.

I visited Bentota beach with a friend I met on holiday. It wasn't as busy as I thought it would be, just a few people who had rented sun loungers like ourselves and some who were taking a stroll or a swim. The beach was vast, very clean and the sea a perfect temperature, although with quite big waves and a strong undercurrent, although I believe it is expected at that time of year. There are showers and toilets but far from five star, so be prepared, and also not much shade. You may have to go to a nearby restaurant for a break from the sun. Overall, an excellent beach. N.B. You may find a stray dog under your Sun lounger trying to seek out some shade but ours was no trouble. It's quite normal for Sri Lanka!
Clear sands and very clean beach!! Excellent Buffet spread and a very well maintained Resort!! Lots of water activities

This is a must see if you are in the bentota area.Soft white sand and the blue sea is a  breathtaking sight.Facilities for water sports are also available.However I like it more as a place to relax and just enjoy the sea and the waves.Best time to visit is early in the morning at the time when the dawn is breaking.There are plenty of sea creatures to see also.I never get tired of this place.
Very nice virgin Beach with wonderful sunset. No much activity but serene and perfect for lazy day out

We spent one night in Sea Rock Hotel, a beach resort which is situated on the Golden Stretch of Beaches in Sri Lanka.  The water was warm and the waves were just brilliant to watch and jump in.  The sands were nice and clean and a paradise for the walkers as well as swimmers.  Wish we had more time to spend on this beach but unfortunately we had a flight to catch.

This is one of the larger beach hotels in the area - rooms surround a courtyard on one side with a balcony and views of the pool and beach on the other.  The hotel Is suitable for a one night-stop-over after a lot of driving of a longer beach holiday. Comfortable outside bars and a patio.  The buffet restaurant has a good variety of items for breakfast and the evening meal.  There is also a small souvenir shop. At times the sea might be suitable for swimming but the pool looks more inviting - nice beach for walks with a few small restaurants in the area.
Nice clean sands.. you  an see islands as well. Watersports are also nearby. Try to book a hotel with private beach. It's worth it.

The Indian Ocean is always so warm, the waves are brilliant to jump and play in.  The beach is long and clean and sandy.  Walking to the right takes you to the rocks and a lovely temple up a short rock path.  Always take a sari and men a T-shirt to cover up when entering a temple.  To the left you can walk past all the hotels including the wonderful Centara Ceysands, and walk through the grass area to take you to the road which you can walk to the town centre on instead of taking the boat ride across the river.

This is one lovely stretch of beach. Must come again We were here just before the monsoon, so it was deserted and we had the entire beach to ourselves. Nice soft sand, mild waves, and an interesting rocky outcrop at either end, for the venturesome, to set out to.
Loved it here, but unable to swim unfortunately, due to unsafe conditions. Some good hotels, carefully concealed by trees etc.
The sea was warm, and lovely to swim in. The walk along the beach was very nice, and easy to reach all restaurants from beach
One of the best beaches ever been, The waters are clear and blue.. Nice place for adventure sports . we did the para motoring .. was fun
Beach is beautiful and lovely for a stroll just watch out for the peoplectrying to sell you excursions

undoubtably a beautiful wide long beach.  You can't swim there and its not safe to leave your belonging untended as there are all sorts of locals hanging around staring at you and trying to sell  you stuff.
Beautiful beach and highly recommended to all visitors. Clean sands and amazing views. We felt as if the beach was reserved for us.
A great beach with clean sands. It is open to public but you won't see many people. Some parts are suitable for swimming while others have rough waves.

Bentota Beach is long public beach, this beach is always full of plastic and other debris, including sharp broken glass, used syringe. locals Dogs and their poo, people bath their dogs, south to Taj hotel there are sewage being dumped in the sea 24/7 via open gutter, also some people have put huts, lounger, restaurant on public beach. Local municipal is making fortune out of tourism tax but not spending any for cleaning beach or look after sewage and other pollution in the sea or any beach maintenance or anything!!. Beware of too much sand flys, crazy dogs, dead animals on beach, keep kids in your watch because their aren't any Life Guards or good First Aid available nearby.

One of the most beautiful beaches of Sri Lanka. Returned after eight years and still found it absolutely breathtaking. Early morning sea was calm and inviting. Watching the sunset on top of a beach rock is the most magical thing you can ever imagine in this little haven.
V were staying at taj, that side f the beach was totally empty, clean , quiet, water was clean. Good to take morning walks.the sand is soft n clean
Beach is average, with many locals and not much structure. The beach could be better cared for, but with the hotel structure behind it, it's a good option for traveling in Sri Lanka

I walked along this beach early every morning and maybe encountered no more than a dozen other early walkers or joggers. There are coloured flags indicating the level of safety for swimming in the sea, I couldn't believe how warm the water was at this time of year.

THIS is one beach you must not visit in this lifetime. One visit and you will say "oh my Goodness, why didn't i think of coming to this place before". so pack up ,book your seat, fly down to Bentota. This is where you meet life for real.

Loved the experience. we were at the Taj Vivanta which is a beach front property. The beach is really clean with clear waters and white sand. Enjoyed the morning walks there with almost the entire beach to ourselves.
Really enjoyed our morning walks along this beautiful beach and lovely clean water to swim in! The temperature was perfect & it wasn't too wild.
The water is a gorgeous temperature and the sand is very fine and powdery. It was a pleasure to walk the full stretch of the beach in the morning

miles of pure clean beach, stare away at a never receeding horizon, well that's what you want on a beach hoiday. Bentota beach provides just that. You wont feel like leaving the place when it turns. Great clean fun and a must do when u visit Sri Lanka
very clean - there was a strong back-current that made bathing difficult for weak swimmers.  The on-shore breeze was very welcome.

We were here during the spring tides (highest high tides and lowest low tides) which created some really good breakers. There is a strong undertow here, but nothing we couldn't cope with.  The sea was wonderfully warm, and the sand was too hot to walk on without flip flops. A beautiful beach - not crowded. If the weather is right, there are beautiful sunsets to enjoy.
This beach is beautiful, and quiet the only negative is all the rubbish (water bottles). The hotel we stayed at was here and perfect. Nice long walks

Bentota beach is beautiful. It has long stretching sand and is pretty clean considering no one appeared to be down cleaning it like they do on the private beaches. There are a few sun beds that you can hire with umbrellas (they quoted us $4 (AUD) for an hour) though we didn't use them. Would definitely need the bed/umbrella if staying for a long time though as the sun has a sting to it. They have an area that is patrolled (red flags). It's pretty quiet too which I am guessing is because of how much beach there is and the time of year (end of April).
Bentota is a lively interesting town. Many hotels,chalets,inns and lots of gems and jewelry shops. Also local handicrafts at reasonable priced

Excellent beach with a few bars. It would be good if the empty water bottles could be removed and certainly tourists should not leave them there. Sun and sand bar is a great place just back from the beach to grab a beer - just over the train track
Good long beach which is great for walks but the beach itself during April at least is just too dangerous and polluted to risk swimming in.
A really nice and clean beach with sand as far as the eye can see. Waves can be strong so don't jump in if you are not a good swimmer.
Large and clean beach with outdoor shower and sunbeds to rent. Great to spend couple of hours on it, but quite hard to swim because of waves

Not too impressed with the beach itself. I went, I looked and I just waked in to cinnamon hotel and spend my time on their green. Walking along the beach road(to the beach, not along the beach) is nice

The beauty of this beach does not come without a price to pay: there are currents and it is very dangerous to swim here. I was once taken to the open ocean within few minutes. Believe me, I was scared - and I consider myself to be experienced and well trained swimmer

A long, quiet beach with plenty of places to stop on the way down. Probably a clean beach for Sri Lanka, but you will find a few pieces of garbage scattered up and down the beach - as well, if you go south of Vivanta (near Wunderbar) you'll find the seafoam is a bit greener than the rest of the beach. There's a river coming down into the ocean that certainly doesn't smell like a river... Good for strolls though.

I travelled alone but was able to walk the beach a number of times each day without any trouble or pestering from people selling things.  Absolutely glorious beach and a stroll along it before breakfast is simply the best way to start the day xx

Lovely beach which for early morning walks you frequently have to yourself. We were staying at the Taj so walked along here most days stopping for a drink at the beach bars. Our favourite became the  Sea view which is before Amal the main beach bar/restaurant and  down a small track. It was lovely to sit and watch the ocean at the hottest part of the day with an occasional train passing beneath us. This place really is a gem and they could not try harder to please. They serve lovely jumbo prawns and you can order them one day and they will have them for you the next. I suspect they cannot afford to buy things they might not sell.A great place for a lunch time snack or just a drink. Lion beers are just 400rupees for a large bottle half the price of the hotel and the view is great even if the stairs up to the restaurant seem a bit of a health and safety risk and crossing the railway track is a bit tricky barefoot. Flip flops a must in my opinion but  his highness says I am being a wimp!!
Gorgeous beach ...not a bad view to wake too I'd never tire....can't wait to be back again.  Fabulous beach party
Beautiful beach, lovely sunsets. You can even have dinner on the beach.We got married on this beach.

This beach rates as one of our top three, expansive golden soft sand that entice you walk the length with great sea breakers rolling together and running gently up the beach. The tides are strong but you have great low surf to play in and the mix of stunning scenery, great surf and sand mixed with 31 degrees of tropical sun shine makes a perfect relaxing day.
Great if you want to have some private time at the huge sand beach, close to cool restaurants and cheap transportation.

so clean & refreshing. Locals come down in the afternoon & play sport & swim people run and walk on the beach in the morning only a few people selling items, I bought some stuff as they are very reasonable. February is a good time to swim, very calm & clean

Bentota Beach is long with fine sand and the beautiful inviting Ocean. At one end there are rocks to sit on and create your own lookout over the beach. There will be vendors offering you lounge chairs to rent and all sorts of things to buy. It can be a bit of a hassle and you end up purchasing things you don't need because you feel sorry for them spending the whole day on the beach without a sale. Also you will come across homeless dogs. I went out of my way to feed them as they were very thin and neglected. Please feed the dogs with a sausage from your breakfast table.
Walking along the beach and watching the water sparkle under the brilliant sunshine on Bentota Beach was absolutely delightful !

Great beach. Really beautiful and not too many vendors bothering you. Good place for beginner and intermediate surfing. The undertow can get quite strong so novice swimmers should proceed with caution. We actually witnessed a woman in need of rescuing for some reason or another. Watch your kids closely here and ask for beach conditions before going in the water.

The sea was rough at the time in October  but it didn't  stop us from dips and swimming. Walking along the beach in the beautiful  warm sunshine and filling in the fresh sea airs  were breathtakingly  marvellous. The hotel Centara Ceysands  had organised a disco night on the beach. It was truly wonderful. We  were able to. arrange a helicopter  ride  by the local  and trusted tour guy  TOK TOK  who organised and arranged a  much excited helicopter  ride and visits to local shops and restaurant also using his TOK TOK commute. I saw one local lady who was picking up litters from the beach.
Beautiful sandy beach.  Great views in both directions of what looks like endless paradise. Locals are friendly and whilst sea is quite rough it's great fun as long as kids are supervised.

Great beach that is very clean and a lovely colour. It was a little choppy while we were there and often the are under currents. This made for ' two red flags' (dangerous conditions). No life guards, only flags before you enter the beach. If you like a cool ocean temperature, you won't find it here. It is still very enjoyable and a reprieve from the heat of the day.
Lovely soft sand, could do with bins as quite a lot if rubbish especially water bottles lying around

A beautiful long stretch of beach. We took to walking along early each morning to build up an appetite for a hearty Sri Lankan Breakfast. What's so lovely is that there are no rows of sun beds and only small pockets of commercial tourist advertising. Totally public so no areas are blocked by hotels.

Unfortunately we didn't pick the best time of the year so we couldn't fully enjoy the sea and snorkeling.. However the surfing bay was good for learning how to surf and the rocky bay there was super fotogenic and full of crabs and lizzards.. There are many hotels and restaurants along the beach as well. Barbara, Czech Republic
The waves are high and great for surfing and playing around It is clean but muddy it is not clear because of the big waves at this season.

The colour of the Waters of the Indian Ocean here is a beautiful pristine blue. What amazed me was the cleanliness maintained on the beach. The waves are good for surfers and a mesmerising sight for non surfers. Of course the sun in Srilanka is torturous so enjoy the early mornings and evenings...the water is soothingly warm. The only minus point is that the sand is extremely fine and soft...great to walk on but the waves bring it up in full force so you can get your mouth full!  I was also lucky to witness a fabulous sunset !  Do make sure you are then in the evening!

This is a beautiful hotel in Bentota right in the centre. It is directly on the beach, has beautiful gardens and a huge pool. The hotel has a kids play area, a pool side restaurant and a buffet restaurant which served great food every day. The room are really nice, the fan is great, AC could be better but bathroom and shower really good. The shower pressure is exceptional. The hotel comes with a huge balcony also. For the money this hotel can't be beat really. It has everything you need for an enjoyable stay. The people and staff can't do enough for you, there are lots of sunbeds and lots of chipmunks running around.
Nice and clean beaches in this part of the world. Water sports and different activities for kids almost every where on the beach.
Not a lot of people.. but loads of choice for hotel and restaurants; it is a bit if a hidden gem as you cannot see  the beach form the road and  all along the road are hotels
Wide beaches all over Sri Lanka, clean sand, warm ocean and lots of bars and restaurants around. Great for long walks and enjoying the breeze.
Beautiful beach to walk along with the surf close by and beautiful sunsets. Surfing available if required.

Sea can get rough but was fine when we were there, need to go beyond breakers to swim, good body surfing in rollers. Does get hot in middle of day so not for lying out on but suitably clothed good for children to play.
Lovely beach clean soft sand, the sea can be dangerous always check the flags. The beach is a public beach so no sunbeds available or umbrellas.
So beautiful and so relaxing.  A lovely atmosphere too. Hotels next to it are luxury and will make your stay near the beach pleasurable. A very good place to experience a beach in Sri Lanka.
One of the cleanest beaches I have seen. Water is green and blue and the beach is very very beautiful. Sunset is worth watching.
This was the first beach I saw in Sri Lanka.. It was very clean crystal clear water and very very scenic. Entire Srilanka is amazingly clean and  I simply loved the beach..
Three local boys drowned the day we arrived!Strong riptide.We did not swim in the sea.There did not appear to be lifeguards on the beach.
Soft sand, warm sea, lovely to take a long walk along.  Nice that there are no hotel sun beds on beach.

Place where you can experience Para Gliding and have some Ayurvedic Medicines along with the Local Cinnamon Tea. People there have very good expertise in planting cinnamon and other herbs. Cinnamon is the main source in Bentota.
Great beach. Town very "local". Market is on a Monday. Temple near by well wort a visit. Used Luba as a guide look up on trip advisor. Highly recommended
The beach at Bentota was a total gem. Far surpassed our expectations. The entire beach was all but deserted at all times, walking the beach at sunset really made our holiday.

Very wide with little amount of people. Easy entrance into the water without any corals or stones. Even in case of big waves it is good to swim near the shore. Great sunsets. *Beware of sunburns like everywhere in Sri Lanka.

One of the nicest beaches to relax and tan. But there are not much activities. Only few restaurants and rental services. It seeme to be oriented more for seniors as there are a lot of big hotel resorts nearby. Ayur Veda experience at Laluna Ayur Veda Centre can be breathtaking.

For a public beach this beach is very clean. I did see an old lady cleaning it , so maybe she is paid by one of the hotels. The beach is not crowded, not too many hackers and overall great. There are some strong currents so be careful when swimming in the ocean.

Had the pleasure of staying literally on Bentota beach during our stay, and it is the most gorgeous natural and unspoilt beach you could imagine, like a perfect Robinson Crusoe tropical island.  Pale golden powder sand beach, hardly any people on it, fringed with palm trees and jungle, and the crashing Indian Ocean.  Sea is not really for swimming in because of the incredibly strong currents and waves, but still great and invigorating to paddle in, plus romantic walks, and breathtaking sunsets.

Stayed at the Avani and walked out onto this beautiful clean beach. Fabulous guy by the Avani called Sammy ( Sammys tours) who arranged some trips for us and was very reliable and trustworthy and costs were reasonable too. We soon realised that not everyone was to be trusted so fantastic to meet Sammy.
Spotlessly clean , great waves, deserted at times, great sunset's, beware can have strong currents, 1 or 2 hawkers that's all, brilliant beach, due to waves ,children need to be supervised.

Stunning in every sense. Quiet, Beautiful and Peaceful. The water is a little rough but good for novice surfers to practice and learn. The mangroves hide all the hotels behind making this place seem extremely private.
This beach area is so beautiful and if you need to dip in the sea make sure you follow the warning flags. Lifeguards are station at the beach run by Sri Lankan Navy.

Bentota beach is beautiful! The 6km beach is divided in two by a small palm area but you can easily walk from end to end. There is no services on the beach (excluding the Hotels along it) and also very few people on it. Perfect for morning runs! On the north end there is a buddhist temple on top of a jungle cliff. During the evening / sun set locals gather to the beach but othervise it is almost deserted considering the location.

For starters: start your Sri Lanka trip with bentota and not columbo or kandy or anywhere else Amongst the umpteen beaches I have been to, this is still on top 3 as of now! If you are lucky, you will spot turtles on the beach! I did 😊 Also, be sure of the water in the morning for its jelly fish infested at some parts..read the signages before you jump into it! Trust me , experience speaks 😊 Feel free to shoot your questions in case you need any details on the stay and things to do
This is a beautiful beach, spotlessly clean and not crowded at all, there were very few hotels along the stretch we stayed on, and no sunbeds clogging up the view
Very clean with very few people on it . Large waves making for a fun time in the water. The sea would not be for unsupervised kids
Very nice beach. Only 4 hotels on 2km. No deck chairs on the beach and only a view vendors Nice location for the sunndowner is Loft in  Avani hotel
Not crowded. No real hassle From hawkers on the beach. Warm water. Little disappointing that no sun beds available on the beach area.

We spent the last three days of our holiday on Bentota Beach. The perfect place to totally relax. The sea was less rough than further south. Plenty of places to stop for a drink, although spaced out. Had to remember our flip flops because the sand was very hot. Great beach.
Lovely quiet beach with postcard like views! Sand is clean and Water is the perfect colour! Not ruined unlike some more commercial beach locations

This beach is famous in Sri Lanka, it is nice and lot's of space, but do not expect much activity apart from sun tanning, swimming and beach walking. mainly locals around there not many tourists!. showers available need a local taxi to get there as most hotels aren't near by.
Nice beach alongside our hotel.  Beautiful walks of a morning and never too busy :)  We enjoyed the beach as it felt natural and not too tampered with, great for dipping but not swimming.
We walked this beach every day of our stay. It is a very clean  with virtually no plastic waste. Certainly at the south end there were very few people.
This beach is long and sandy and during our stay in February, not busy. The sea is clean and warm. Lovely for a nice peaceful walk.

Very quite strand, not so crowded...there are some big hotels in front of the beach, but this is not bad, because they are a bit in the background and not.very high...and so there are not even a shop or a restaurant beside each other..that keeps the beach really naturally. But therefore you have to take snacks and water or what ever you want with you, because there are no shops at the beach.
This is a lovely clean beach with stunning views and lovely warm ocean waves. Not recommended for swimming but lovely for a paddle. Lovely sunsets too
Super clean sandy beach worth visiting. 4km of white soft sand. great surf and lovely to swim in. very quiet beach hardly anyone uses it even in high season
This beach seems to go on forever!  Very wide in most parts of the beach.  There are a number of restaurant/bars along the beach, as well as some large hotels and resorts.

Beautiful beach. Be warned that if you are female in a swim suit and chose to swim between the flags where it is safer, there will be a lot of locals and you will be looked at. Found this out the hard way.
Be very careful where you swim, there are rip tides so swim where there are flags/life guards. There are some alcoves where it appeared to be safer to swim, a bit calmer.

The beach provides a wide expanse of sandy a thing area with wonderful sunsets. One thing to remember when swimming is the strong undercurrent which can be treacherous as one person had died an in accident the the previous week.
A very clean and tidy beach, also very quiet, no beach shacks, we have travelled to India for almost 30 years, so this was a pleasant shock. This place is definitely worth a visit.
Bentota Beach is a wide and large beach with soft sand and a warm sea. Great for sunsets! We stayed in a hotel (Centara Ceysands) just by the beach and it was great!
Soft sand and very clean,  not too busy and very peaceful.  Waves can be a little rough at times.  Loved it.
Lovely clean beach set on a long bay with the Indian Ocean to swim or paddle in. Not too many hawkers trying to sell you things you don't really need either!!

This is a long, straight beach with a slowly sloping drop so there is little in the way of undertow here. The waves are fairly gentle and in three days I didn't see any get above a half metre. I saw a couple of SUPs and one board rider but they didn't have much luck with long rides. As you know, beach conditions change by the day. There was a gentle sweep to the north and little in the way of a rip along the stretch we were in. The beach itself is very nice, pretty clean and wide.

The beach has glorious sand, lovely warm water and very few people when we went in March 2017. It is peaceful as businesses are not allowed to operate directly on the beach so you do have to walk to nearby businesses by the railtrack for food and drink.

Open to the public. A very long thin expanse of golden sand backed by thin jungle. Basically left to sunbathe and enjoy the warm sea with little disturbance. Depending were one was on the beach away from the centres no bars or food outlets - just sea and beach.
Clean beach with choice of places to eat, boat rides if you want them and not far from major beachside hotels. Safe for swimming good place to spend the day.
Fine sandy beach easy to walk on bare feet.sea bit choppy but safe if flag colours danger signsfollowed.Deep sea diving ,helicopter rides ,motorised gliding facilities available.

This is the type of beach that goes for miles - it is clean and safe and great for running and long walks. There are hotels and restaurants all the way along  ( but set back and mostly hidden in forest) so the beach is used by both locals and tourists.  It was never crowded, even on a public holiday. We spent a lot of time jumping waves and swimming every day. It was great to mix a few days of beach with a few days of sightseeing.
We were here on 12/3/16 and, unlike other reviewers, found the beach to be very clean.   The water was warm, and the surf fun for wave jumping, etc.  Not too many vendors either.
Nice beach ruined by pollution from toxic streams from mainland and careless littering. Sort it out Sri Lanka

Accessing the Bentota Beach is slightly tricky from Rockery Villa hotel as you have to walk through a small path between houses which are being renovated, but the beach is great. First, you cross a railtrack (you can see trains every hour or so, speed is about 50km/h), then you go through palm trees and mangroves (you can benefit from their shade) and then you have a large sand beach with nice waves, fun for teens. Few tourists, few sellers who are nice people actually (if you know prices in regular shops, you can buy from them cheaper) If you look for a beautiful natural beach that is suitable for a trainspotter and/or a shopping addict, this is the place... ;-)

This is absolutely stunning.    Long stretches of golden sand.   Only downside, is that people should treat it with respect and take their rubbish with them.  But otherwise it is lovely, suitable for children if supervised.

It's really good place to relax. Not so many tourist and the beach is almost empty whole day. You can try to swim but the waves are huge. But Sri-Lanka isn't place for good ocean swimming. So you have to go to Bentota Beach to see this beauty.
my hotel had a private beach. makes the beach less crowded. you can go for a swim when the tide is safe. not a clear beach but it surely is fun.

Great beach that due to its length gives a good reason to stretch your legs has a fairly undulating feature set that goes from shallow to chest high then shallow again etc which gives a large area for a dip.
Why don't the local authorities recognise the importance of tourism, and not to mention a bit of self pride, and clean this beach. Great if the indolent stray dogs could be relocated or put down too.
You can walk hours on the beach, alias beaches as you can extend your walk over next beaches. Go walking, up you're tired and back by tuk-tuk. Even in December-January high season, we saw few people.

We visited Sri Lanka for a month last year. This beach takes some beating as it is clean, quiet, beautiful sand and warm sea. You have to adhere to sea safety as there can be strong currents further out.
A clean, peaceful beach with lots of accommodation choices nearby. Worth a visit for a relaxing time.

This is how a beach should look like: free of human touch. There are no chairs, no umbrellas, just people walking and enjoying Indian Ocean (waves are very strong, so not a good place to bathe). I hope it will stay clean in the future, although the contrary signs are already creeping in...
Perfect for early morning walks. Local fishermen casting their nets and bringing in the catch. Strong currents.
The sea is dangerous ,one man drowned during our holiday, with plenty of under currents.OK for paddelling
We loved body boarding in the warm sea- not crazy waves so perfect for my 3 and 6 year old! The beach was so quiet in the day. It was busiest at sunset time- for good reason, stunning

Bentota beach is a beautiful, long stretch of sand still lacking the normal tourist area byproducts - seas of sun beds, trash and beach vendors. A paradise compared to Hikkaduwa! Perfect for early morning running and swimming amidst the waves - which are always present (stay safe and respect the flags).
Quiet, clean, warm waters, and fabulous for swimming. There are private sunbeds but you can use them even if you are not staying at the hotels. Very few hotels tucked away from the beach

Whilst on holiday at Centara Ceysands we used this beach for walking every day. It is quite unspoilt although there is some discrete tourist activities i.e. surfing lessons and parasailing etc. Helicopter rides and be mildly intrusive. Beach salesmen are not rude or aggressive and a polite " No thank you " will normally suffice
Long white beach. This beach was very peaceful and clean. Waves were big but not too big. Worth to see.

The beach was clean and the water condition was good. The waves can pick up as we went in late Dec. But still good to play around 10 to 20 meters from shore. The beach does get very dark at night with no lighting. But very safe.
Clean and surprisingly few tourists.  Water lovely and warm though it is a public beach - no lifeguards
Did a walk along the beach - could not swin due to a heavy swell.  Golden sands, blue water, very beautiful.  Not busy at all.
Beach is large, water is very clear, sand is thin; beautiful waves,no beach beds or coffe shops - is possible to stay with towel beach from hotel
we went to visit Bentota beach while going to the market and it is a beautiful sandy beach very soft sand well worth a visit
Absolutely beautiful beach, and only a few hotels lay above it so large parts are mostly empty of people. Before sunset lots of locals gather to socialize and play games, making it come alive.

This is a lovely stretch of beach. You will see locals and tourists alike enjoying this place but it is big enough that it does not get crowded. Golden sand, nice water. Couple of bars/restaurants nearby
Nice beach and not crowded. Could go swimming in some parts. We experienced larger waves in Bentota compared to Mirissa. However, no beach bars/ restaurants.
Superb sun rise and sunset, great long stretch of golden sands and warm Indian Ocean one side and the Bentota river the other.
A lovely sandy beach for walking undisturbed early mornings before the heat of the day or evenings to enjoy the sun setting.

This is a public beach, but it is long and wide and has very few people.  The water is gorgeous.  Warm and clear.  Nice waves.  It's a great walking beach with hard packed and level sand near the water.
This is a beautiful unpolluted Sri Lankan beach. It's a great stop inbetween Galle and Colombo with not many people or tourists. There are cheap guest houses around.
Good clean beach without crowds.  Families enjoying the sea, joggers, walkers, paddlers. Just what you want.
Loved the sand! The rocks give such a character to the beach! There's a lagoon on the side of Taj Vivanta. Dont forget to spend sometime there.
It is a clean and peaceful beach with not much crowd and I guess that is what what looks forward to.

It's a very nice long stretch of beach - great for long walks. Bustling with people in the evening. Suggest that precaution is taken when taking young kids into the sea as it can get a bit choppy few meters inside.

We stayed 2 weeks resort next  to beach andå regulary walked and swim here. Easy beach to walk, clean and not too much commercial. Wawes are easy and you van go saimming to wawes. Not good place for snorkeling due wawes and visibility. End on beach area next to river lots of crabs and ole temple. Helicopter field and opportunity to take flight if indrested.
A beautiful beach close to Centara Resort and Spa. You can really enjoy walking for miles on this beach and view some spectacular sunsets.

With lots of Restaurant along side the beach you can surely have a great time diving and enjoying the Sea. Its very clean and good place to chill out with friends either in the sea or on the beach restaurant having some drinks.
Great beach and fun views! Amazing to take a stroll here during sunset, highly recommended and a must do!
It is indeed a very clean beach with nice sand. The waves are very strong but when carefull you enjoy jumping on those.

If you like to be alone on a great beach, this is one of them. South of "the centre of Bentota" (there really isnt much of a centre), the beach stretches on, with very few people. Great sand, great to watch the sunset, and just very beautiful.
Big, nice beach. Ocean is great, bug waves but safe. The sand is perfect. Actually everything is perfect. My kind od beach.
The sand is soft and great for kids.  The view is breathtaking and the vast horizon looking out from the beach is amazing.  Not to mention the sunsets
Spent most of the time riding the huge waves hawkers can be a nuisance but are not persistent has a beach bar

Great beach guilt clean and in good condition with a number of sellers who will offer you trips from fishing to river trips and helicopter rides. The guy we used was a guy called Ajith and he is is easily recognisable as he looks like Errol Brown from hot chocolate real nice guy and not a rip of artist

This is a nice beach with adventure sports like para gliding around 2 hours' drive (via the Galle Expressway) from Colombo city. The beach is neat and well maintained. It is certainly worth a visit in case you want to be away from the hustle and bustle of the city in the evenings. You can relax here and we found this was not crowded between 3-6 pm when we visited.

One of the most clean and beautiful beaches I have been. And not crowded during this time. Weekends get little bit busy of locals but still fun. People here is humble friendly and easily you can start a short conversation all you need is a smile on your face. Hope that's helpful :)
A beautiful serene beach with less crowd and clear blue water. It is a perfect place to watch the sunset.
Great for an afternoon stroll but check the warning flags for the sea state before swimming. The sand is quite invigorating on the feet

Plenty of space if you are prepares to walk a little way from the hotels. Beds & shades available but you'll need to take a drink. Water is very refreshing but some bits have a big undercurrent- be careful
Very beautiful beach with very few people. Calm and serene. No facilities/action on beach, so go prepared.

A nice quite beach in sri lanka. If you wish to avoid the crowded location like hikkaduwa then this is a very good option. Not as commercialised as Hikkaduwa, this is the place for a nice quite holiday.
Yellow sands, very few shells and very few people.    Occasional fishing canoes with their outrigger floats waiting for their lobster fishing crew to man them.

Nice beach, lots of sand and lots of big waves! For the week we stayed in Bentota there were 2 red flags on the beach, stating it was dangerous to enter the tide due to strong currents etc. It was certainly rough, but good fun jumping the waves!
Just very beautiful and not many tourist at the time I was there. Nice water temperatur and perfect for long beach walkes.
One of the best beaches in Sri Lanka. Very clean and well maintained. Go ahead and get into the water unhesitatingly. Perfect for a walk/jog, too.

This is a most beautiful beach, wide and with golden sand that you can make sandcastles with. It is extraordinarily quiet an stretches for two and a half kilometres between the headlands. It is far better than walking along the road if you want to access the delightful beach cafes. We even walked along at night from the resort we were staying in to another about 300 metres along where we had dinner.

You cannot fault the beach as photos show.  However as a family of 3 (one 27 year old) it was not for us.  It's probably fine if you are in one of the large hotels on the beach on an all inclusive basis. The beach lacked any bars/cafes/places of interest or atmosphere with very few people actually on the beach (and it was peek time).There were also very few layout beds or umbrellas mostly people seem to stay in their hotel complexes.  We spent a pleasant day here but much preferred Hikkaduwa & Mirissa beaches.
We just wanted to be by the beach all day and Bentota offered the perfect beaches!  Smooth, clean sand and water. Highly recommended.
Cleaner sand & water but the waves could get faster and stronger after 6 pm. Sunset is the best to watch for 👍

Good place to visit. Very good clean beach. Also don't miss to visit turtle hatchery. There some good selection of hotels, the surf, cinnamon. Try to see if there is any Facebook offers on one of these before booking. I hope you'll enjoy out there for sure!
The beach is quiet and clean with plenty of space to sunbath and play beach game.  The sea is rough so take care when swimming.  Beautiful sunsets!

The beach in Bentota wasn't the most beautiful I've seen, but it was pretty none the less and clean. Also very quiet with no hawkers - so very relaxing. It's also really safe, with no noticeable rips during our stay.
The Sri Lanka's most famous beach and love to spend time in this beach and beach has a beautiful succession of gentle, curved bays backed by the large lagoon of the Bentota River.
Perfect for walking, swimming, relaxing. The morning is the best time before the wind comes up. Some tasty eating places with fresh juice too.
I love this wonderful Beach. I been there now a couple times and it is always a beautiful pleasure to visit.

this beach is just awesome. You have to go there when in Sri Lanka. It´s quiet, not crowded at all, the waves are big but safe because the water is not higher than 1 meter to pretty logn distance from the shore. It´s safe there however the waves looks dangerous. It was really breathtaking. You can just sit there and look at the ocean for the whole day without anyone interrupting. We only left to eat to some close bar which we found close to our place on the beach and then went back. :)
Excellent beach with amazingly safe waves beautiful sand. Not bothered by people trying to sell items easy to say no !!!

Lovely beach. The slope is very gradual so one can walk really far into the sea and still remain in knee deep water. The beach is clean and not very crowded. The water temperature was ideal. In all excellent.
Nice beach with only a few good hotels on.  The beach us clean on one half but dirty with rubbish on the other half. A nice beach for 3 days only.

Good beach very clean. No facilities such as sunbeds parasols or lifeguards. If your hotel is on the beach then great. You will be troubled by locals selling wares but if your polite and say no thanks they pass on bu

One of the most beautiful n pristine beaches you will ever come across. The sand on the beach is extremely soft, just like soft candy balls! The water is very clear n you can see all shades of blue in water. The other good thing about the bentota is that the sea is shallow till a good distance, which is a good thing for nom swimmers like me- you can go a long distance into the sea, without the fear of drowning. The beach is not crowded but is also not empty at this time of the year. Its a must visit place when you are visiting Srilanka!

We thought that Bentota Beach was to be crowded with oily sunbathing tourists, but my....were we wrong! We could walk a couple of miles along the Beach without bumping into any other people. There were sandbeds there allright, but the local hotel establishments are not allowed to drag them to the Waters edge, which is fantastic. This is such a cool Beach if you are lokking for Peace and calm and Bounty atmosphere.
best for all local and tourist for enjoy their pleasure freedom vacation.everything are ok.great day
Best beach in sri lanka- soft white sands, good surf and amazing sunsets. Beautiful. Water sports available and some great bars along.
Discover Bentota Beach: a serious contender for a beach holiday, no matter what your budget

Bentota Beach is a flat, long clean beach.  The water temperature in December/January was about 28 degrees.  The locals did approach you with their goods to sell but a "no thanks" and they left you alone.

We stayed here for new year's. It is one of the most happening places of Sri Lanka. There are lot of beach shacks to have good food and conversation. To top it off, the crowd here is amazing. Don't give this place a miss!
We took many sunset walks along this beach, its really beautiful. Not much to do - no sunbed sellers/ cafes/ wcs etc, but thats why we loved it :)

A friend and I stayed at Club Villa and ventured onto the beach several times. Most people appear to stay by their hotel pools, so it was relatively quiet. It's a nice clean beach, and swimmable (compared to our stay in Tangalle, where the turf was very rough and difficult to manage). Have a walk up and down and see the various hotels and venues. The most annoying aspect was a hawker from Wunderbar, who approached us a few times about having lunch, dinner, drinks, etc. at the venue. He didn't just approach, he also hovered. The net effect was that we wanted NOT to go there. Otherwise, this is a great beach.
Lovely spread of open beach, kept beautifully clean.  Little hassle.  reasonable for swimming; excellent for walking or jogging
Nice clean beach with nice waves and nice sundowner we have been here for one week. Near Avani hotel.
One of the best around the area and not packed with tourists. Loved it here, just be careful of the currents.

Very glad we experienced Bentota beach before we left Sri Lanka as it was a welcome contrast to some of the busy, noisy, 'party' beaches we had been staying on further south. Bentota as long and quite empty - it benefits from all the resort developments being set back away from the actual beach itself so it feels more remote than it actually is. The sea was quite rough but quite warm when we were there. Too rough for children I expect. The only reason I deduct a star is for the litter which I saw accumulated on various piles under the mangrove trees. I hope someone comes to collect this as it spoils the beauty of the beach and is dangerous for wildlife.

Another beautiful beach in The Southern Province - just too hot even for sunbathers .... I stopped off at Bentota Beach for a few minutes only given the heat. Not too many people on the beach but lovely and scenic and good for surfers.
The backwaters in Bentota was just amazing. It really takes you back in time and makes you feel that you are in the 70s.

This beach is amazing! the sand is soft and golden and you can walk for miles! At one end there is a friendly little coconut seller who loved my tshirt so much i let him keep it! At the other end there is a beautiful spice garden with a buddhist temple hidden within. Be careful on this beach though.. you might just end up taking a helicoptor flight and a paragliding flight! It looked fun and was fun! The sea was warm and we had a great time  swimming in the waves.
Lovely place to walk , run or just admire the scenery a lovely quiet long beach Swimming not always advisable strong currents but this place is well worth a visit
